data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old Irish 'padraig', meaning 'noble, generous, and valiant'. The name Peadar has a rich history in Irish mythology as the name of several legendary figures. The name Peadar carries the meaning “Brave” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Peadar usually hope their child will grow to embody brave and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Peadar belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Brave.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Peadar total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.
data.cultural_impact: Peadar is a name with a deep roots in Irish culture. In mythology, there are several Peadars, including St. Peadar, the patron saint of Corfu and Minella (very likely transferred from an earlier Irish deity), and Peadar O'Donnell, a prominent 20th-century Irish revolutionary leader. This name continues to resonate within the Irish and larger Catholic communities, and it is a source of pride and connection to their history and heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Peadar signifies the ideals of a noble, generous, and valiant spirit. It is a reminder to strive for the strength and virtue embodied by the legendary Irish figures who shared this name. For those looking for a spiritual influence in their lives, the name Peadar may symbolize a commitment to acts of charity, generosity, and bravery, following in the footsteps of the saintly and historical figures who are associated with this name.
